stemMd: What is the main lesson of the map discrepancy?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Accessibility can be inferred from distance alone.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Formal representations should be checked against actual use and varied needs.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Official maps should never be consulted.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The shortest path is always the only route worth recording.

explanationMd: The discrepancy prompted observation that added both the shortcut and its limitations to the picture. The passage favours combining formal information with lived use, rather than rejecting either source or relying on distance alone.

distractorRationale.d: The passage says maps can guide inquiry.
distractorRationale.e: Both routes and their conditions were documented.
distractorRationale.c: A site visit was used to confirm and refine them.
distractorRationale.a: The site visit revealed why distance was insufficient.
